newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ to become LHTEC helicopter service centre.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ to become LHTEC helicopter service centre.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd and the Light Helicopter Turbine Co (LHTEC) of the United States on Monday said Air NZ would become a LHTEC service centre for engines used in the GKN Westland Super Lynx helicopter.
Air NZ said new maritime helicopters are about to be ordered by the Royal Australian Navy and Royal New Zealand Navy.
The Super Lynx, which is under consideration, is a two-crew, multi-role helicopter, purpose designed for operations from small ships in severe weather.
Over 350 Lynx are in service worldwide.

The establishment of a LHTEC heavy maintenance service centre in Australasia would enable the repair, overhaul and testing of the CTS800-4N engine to be carried out locally. The engine resulted from investment by the U.S. Department of Defense and LHTEC in the U.S. Army's Comanche programme.
Air NZ Engineering Services already provides services for the Australian Defence Force and the New Zealand Ministry of Defence.
LHTEC is a partnership between Allied Signal Inc and the Allison Engine Co of the U.S.
Air NZ said the strategic relationship between LHTEC and Air NZ should result in a further expansion of Air NZ's engineering business and present future opportunities in South East Asia.
